answer: According to the clinical guidelines from MedlinePlus (U.S. National Library of Medicine, 2024), an A1C level below 5.7% is considered normal, between 5.7-6.4% indicates prediabetes, and 6.5% or higher indicates diabetes. Unlike a daily finger-stick blood glucose test that shows blood sugar at a particular moment in time, the A1C test reflects your average blood sugar level over the past few months. Therefore, for individuals transitioning from a normal A1C to prediabetes, a significant increase is observed, often correlating with a gradual elevation above 5.7% over time. It's important to note that this threshold needs clinical review before any definitive diagnosis. [MedlinePlus (U.S. National Library of Medicine), 2024]

results.content: The A1C (or HbA1c) test shows average blood sugar levels over the past 2-3 months. An A1C below 5.7% is normal, 5.7-6.4% indicates prediabetes, and 6.5% or higher indicates diabetes. Unlike a daily finger-stick, A1C reflects a longer-term trend rather than a single moment.
results.citation: The A1C Test and Diabetes, MedlinePlus (U.S. National Library of Medicine), 2024

result.disclaimer: Evidence excerpts for professional review; not a diagnosis.
